questions.question_text: Smallest rotational angle for a regular pentagon is:
A non-square rectangle has how many lines of symmetry?
State lines of symmetry and smallest rotational angle for an equilateral triangle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Lines of symmetry = 3. Smallest rotational angle = 360° / 3 = 120°.

questions.question_text: Can a figure have rotational symmetry with smallest angle 17°? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No, because 360° / 17 = 21.176... (360° is not an exact integer multiple of 17°).

questions.question_text: Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes. Find its lines of symmetry and smallest rotational angle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Lines of symmetry = 24. Order of rotational symmetry = 24. Smallest angle = 360° / 24 = 15°.

questions.question_text: Explain why a non-square rectangle's diagonal is NOT a line of symmetry.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Folding a rectangle along its diagonal causes opposite vertices to overhang rather than overlap perfectly.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Ceiling Fan Blade Rotational Symmetry. A ceiling fan has 6 identical blades arranged symmetrically.
(a) What is its order of rotational symmetry? (2 marks)
(b) List all rotation angles less than 360° where it looks identical to start position. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Order = 6.
(b) Smallest angle = 360° / 6 = 60°. Rotation angles: 60°, 120°, 180°, 240°, 300°.

questions.question_text: Order of rotational symmetry of a square is:
Number of lines of symmetry in a regular hexagon is:
Find smallest angle of rotational symmetry for a regular octagon.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Order = 8. Smallest angle = 360° / 8 = 45°.

questions.question_text: Name three English capital letters that have both vertical and horizontal lines of symmetry.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Letters H, I, O, X.

questions.question_text: State lines of symmetry and order of rotational symmetry for a circle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Lines of symmetry = Infinitely many (any diameter line). Rotational symmetry = Infinite order (symmetric at any rotation angle).

questions.question_text: Differentiate between Line (Reflection) Symmetry and Rotational Symmetry with examples.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Line symmetry involves reflection across a axis causing fold halves to overlap (e.g. Isosceles triangle). Rotational symmetry involves turning a shape around a center point to match original appearance before 360° (e.g. Windmill).

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Tile Motif Symmetry Analysis. A square floor tile features a 4-fold symmetric lotus design.
(a) State number of reflection lines and order of rotational symmetry. (2 marks)
(b) If tile is rotated by 90°, 180°, 270°, describe its appearance relative to 0°. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Lines of symmetry = 4. Order of rotational symmetry = 4.
(b) Due to 4-fold symmetry, the tile looks EXACTLY IDENTICAL to its original 0° position at 90°, 180°, and 270°.

questions.question_text: Which letter possesses ONLY vertical line symmetry?
Smallest rotational angle for a shape with order 3 is:
Find lines of symmetry for an isosceles triangle and a scalene triangle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Isosceles triangle = 1 line of symmetry. Scalene triangle = 0 lines of symmetry.

questions.question_text: What is the order of rotational symmetry for an S-shaped icon?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Order = 2 (matches at 180° and 360°).

questions.question_text: A figure has rotational symmetry angles of 45°, 90°, 135°, 180°, 225°, 270°, 315°, 360°. Find its order.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Order = count of symmetric angles = 8. Smallest angle = 45°.

questions.question_text: Explain paper folding test for checking line symmetry of a drawn shape.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Draw shape on paper, fold along candidate axis line. If two halves coincide completely with zero overhang, the fold line is a true line of symmetry.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Traffic Signboard Symmetry. Analyze symmetry of 3 traffic signs: (1) Stop sign (regular octagon), (2) Yield sign (equilateral triangle), (3) Speed limit sign (rectangle).
(a) State lines of symmetry for each sign. (2 marks)
(b) Find smallest rotational angle for sign (1) and sign (2). (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Regular octagon = 8 lines; Equilateral triangle = 3 lines; Rectangle = 2 lines.
(b) Octagon = 360° / 8 = 45°. Equilateral triangle = 360° / 3 = 120°.

questions.question_text: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus (non-square) have?
If a shape matches its position 5 times in a full turn, its order is:
Find smallest rotational angle for a regular 10-gon (decagon).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Order = 10. Smallest angle = 360° / 10 = 36°.

questions.question_text: Name two digits from 0-9 that possess rotational symmetry of order 2.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Digits 0 and 8.

questions.question_text: Draw a figure with 2 lines of symmetry but NO rotational symmetry order > 1.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: An isosceles trapezium or a symmetrical tree icon with distinct top and bottom.

questions.question_text: Show why an isosceles triangle has 1 line of symmetry but rotational symmetry order of only 1.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Fold along altitude bisects base into mirror halves (1 line of symmetry). Rotating around center does not match original shape until a full 360° turn (Order = 1, no proper rotational symmetry).

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Snowflake Crystal Geometry. A natural hexagonal snowflake crystal exhibits 6-fold symmetry.
(a) State its lines of symmetry and order of rotational symmetry. (2 marks)
(b) Calculate all rotational angles between 0° and 360°. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Lines of symmetry = 6. Order of rotational symmetry = 6.
(b) Rotational angles = 60°, 120°, 180°, 240°, 300° (and 360°).

questions.question_text: Which shape has rotational symmetry order > 1 but NO line symmetry?
Angle of rotational symmetry for a 2-blade propeller is:
Find lines of symmetry of a regular nonagon (9 sides).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Regular 9-gon has 9 lines of symmetry.

questions.question_text: Can a triangle have 2 lines of symmetry? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No! A triangle can have 0 (scalene), 1 (isosceles), or 3 (equilateral) lines of symmetry. It can never have exactly 2 lines.

questions.question_text: Calculate smallest rotational angle for a 12-pointed star icon.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Order = 12. Smallest angle = 360° / 12 = 30°.

questions.question_text: Explain line and rotational symmetry properties of a kite polygon.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A kite has exactly 1 line of symmetry (along its main diagonal connecting non-equal angle vertices). Rotational symmetry order = 1 (no proper rotational symmetry).

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Logo Design Analysis. A company logo consists of 4 identical overlapping circles arranged symmetrically around a center point O.
(a) Identify lines of reflection symmetry and order of rotational symmetry. (2 marks)
(b) If design is rotated by 45°, does it match original position? Explain. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Lines of symmetry = 4. Order of rotational symmetry = 4.
(b) Smallest rotational angle = 360° / 4 = 90°. At 45°, it does NOT match original position because 45° is not a multiple of 90°.

questions.question_text: State lines of symmetry and rotational angle for equilateral triangle.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: 3 lines of symmetry; smallest angle = 360/3 = 120°. [2 Marks]

questions.question_text: Why can't a shape have smallest rotational angle of 17°?
How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: Infinitely many lines (every diameter is a symmetry line). [2 Marks]

questions.question_text: Find rotational order for 4-blade windmill.
Give 2 real-life examples of line symmetry.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: Butterfly wings, Taj Mahal facade. [2 Marks]

questions.question_text:
(a) Compare lines of symmetry for square vs non-square rectangle. (2 Marks)
(b) Compare their orders of rotational symmetry. (2 Marks)
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:
(a) Square has 4 (2 midsegments + 2 diagonals); Rectangle has 2 (midsegments only). [2 Marks]
(b) Square rotational order = 4 (90°); Rectangle rotational order = 2 (180°). [2 Marks]

(b) List all rotation angles less than 360° for regular octagon. (2 Marks)
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:

(b) Smallest angle = 45°. Angles: 45°, 90°, 135°, 180°, 225°, 270°, 315°. [2 Marks]
